conceptRelations.notes: Equivalence concerns the genus circumscription represented by the two sources; it does not convert Schubert's provisional Saitis-group placement into an accepted placement.
conceptRelations.rationale: The Lucid and Schubert treatments share the same type species, Barraina anfracta, and the same six-species composition: B. abbedar, B. anfracta, B. banyabba, B. melanoros, B. occidentalis and B. pilata. Schubert questions the genus's monophyly and Saitis-group placement, but does not propose a different circumscription for the named genus concept.

conceptRelations.notes: Equivalence does not imply that Frewena is a confirmed member of the Saitis group.
conceptRelations.rationale: Both sources anchor Frewena to F. maculata and include the same two species, F. maculata and F. terraregina. Schubert leaves monophyly, boundaries and Saitis-group placement provisional but does not replace the genus circumscription with another named concept.

sourceComponent.rationale: Lucid itself suggests that Australian H. albovittatum sensu Keyserling represents the missing male of Maratus scutulatus; Schubert restores that species to Hypoblemum. This is a cross-source inference, not an explicit synonymy in the thesis.
The relevant Schubert revision does not explicitly dispose of the Lucid H. villosum name usage.

conceptRelations.notes: Do not use the identical genus spelling to collapse these concepts. The restoration and combinations proposed in the thesis are not formally published under the ICZN merely by appearing there.
conceptRelations.rationale: The Lucid entity deliberately retains Hypoblemum but describes a confused two-name concept based on H. villosum and H. albovittatum, including an assertion that Australian material called H. albovittatum may be the missing male of Maratus scutulatus. Schubert restores a type-anchored Hypoblemum containing H. griseum, H. magnum, H. scutulatum and H. unicum, and synonymises Saitis taeniatus with H. griseum. The shared generic name and probable scutulatum connection support overlap, but the source compositions and name usages are not equivalent.

sourceComponent.rationale: These species are included under Jotus in both sources.
Schubert explicitly lists both as doubtful generic placements rather than accepted members of the revised genus.

conceptRelations.notes: Tropijotus fortiniae was transferred from Jotus in the thesis, but it is not listed in the Lucid Jotus fact-sheet composition. No Lucid-Jotus-to-Tropijotus component mapping is fabricated from historical genus placement alone.
conceptRelations.rationale: The two concepts share the type species and five accepted species: J. auripes, J. braccatus, J. frosti, J. minutus and J. remus. Schubert's Chapter IV concept is broader in accepted composition and transfers three species from Maratus, while J. debilis and J. insulanus, accepted in Lucid, are treated as of doubtful generic placement. The later concept therefore overlaps substantially but is not coextensive with the Lucid entity.

sourceComponent.rationale: Representative Lucid-listed species retained in Schubert's Maratus sensu stricto; the target list is illustrative rather than a second complete composition.

conceptRelations.notes: This mapping records Schubert's thesis treatment as a concept reconciliation. The proposed new genera and combinations are not formally published under the ICZN merely by appearing in the thesis. Lucid labels, including apparent spelling inconsistencies, remain unmodified.
conceptRelations.rationale: Lucid explicitly defines Maratus as a composite of peacock spiders and unrevised species inherited through the synonymised Lycidas. Schubert restricts Maratus sensu stricto and explicitly reallocates named members of the Lucid list to Anablemum, Hypoblemum, Jotus, Micromaratus, Salinatus, Striattus and Variattus. Lucid Maratus is therefore a broad legacy concept split across eight later biological concepts, not an equivalent of TC0007.

sourceComponent.rationale: Shared type species.

The thesis declares the name a nomen dubium. Because the controlled crosswalk vocabulary has no nomen-dubium relationship, unresolved is used without converting that status into incertae sedis; the exact status is retained here and in TC0020.

conceptRelations.notes: Identical genus spelling and a shared type species do not erase the changed status of non-type contents.
conceptRelations.rationale: Both concepts are anchored to Margaromma funestum. Lucid also accepts M. obscurum while already warning that it likely does not belong in the genus; Schubert treats M. obscurum as a nomen dubium, adds other doubtful names, and states that Margaromma is poorly defined and needs type re-examination. The type-linked concepts overlap, but their accepted and unresolved contents are not equivalent.

conceptRelations.notes: TC0023 (cf. Prostheclina sp.) remains an unresolved separate lineage and is not included in this mapping.
conceptRelations.rationale: Both sources use Prostheclina pallida as the type anchor and list the same seven described species: P. amplior, P. basilonesa, P. boreoaitha, P. boreoxantha, P. bulburin, P. eungella and P. pallida. Schubert's separately modelled cf. Prostheclina lineage is not forced into the genus and therefore does not broaden this equivalence.

sourceComponent.rationale: The Lucid Australian contents do not include the three species retained in Schubert's Saitis sensu stricto.

conceptRelations.notes: The mapping is a split with unresolved residues, not a transfer of the Lucid entity wholesale. Thesis-only combinations and synonymies retain the nomenclatural caveat recorded in 04_taxon_concepts.json.
conceptRelations.rationale: The Lucid entity is an Australian holding concept containing S. insectus, S. insulanus, S. lacustris, S. magniceps, S. mutans, S. signatus, S. taeniatus and S. virgatus. Schubert's Saitis sensu stricto is instead restricted provisionally to the Mediterranean type species S. barbipes plus S. graecus and S. tauricus. None of those three occurs in the Lucid Australian list. Schubert transfers S. mutans to Variattus, synonymises S. taeniatus with Hypoblemum griseum, synonymises S. virgatus with Umbrattus bimaculatus, and leaves or declares several other Lucid names unresolved or dubious. The concepts are therefore explicitly not equivalent and the legacy contents have multiple later dispositions.

sourceComponent.rationale: The Lucid description explicitly concerns Australian species and not the type-species-anchored Salpesia sensu stricto.
Explicit thesis transfer; Saitis virgatus is treated as its junior synonym.
The thesis declares both names nomina dubia; no defensible destination concept exists.
The thesis treats it as incertae sedis and recovers it as sister to Servaea, not as a member of a revised Servaea concept.

conceptRelations.notes: The Salpesia name is shared, but the source concepts are expressly different. The internally conflicting Umbrattus type-species assertions remain unresolved in TC0014 and are not adjudicated here.
conceptRelations.rationale: The Lucid fact sheet explicitly says its entity describes four misplaced Australian species rather than the Seychelles type species Salpesia soricina. Schubert likewise finds no evidence that those Australian usages are congeneric with the type. Salpesia bimaculata is transferred to Umbrattus and treated as the senior synonym of Saitis virgatus; S. bicolor and S. villosa become nomina dubia, while S. squalida is incertae sedis and recovered sister to Servaea. The Lucid entity is therefore not equivalent to Schubert's type-anchored Salpesia concept and has no single later destination.

conceptRelations.notes: Reviewed because of the explicit phylogenetic result, but intentionally left without a target concept rather than fabricating coverage.
conceptRelations.rationale: Schubert uses Servaea as an external phylogenetic comparator and recovers Salpesia squalida as its sister, but does not revise, diagnose or delimit a Servaea genus concept in Chapters III-V. No Servaea concept exists in 04_taxon_concepts.json, and a sister relationship involving one misplaced species is not evidence that the Lucid Servaea entity should be merged with or expanded to include it.

encoding.reconstruction_rule: For each state_id and each taxon_id in taxon_ids order, use the explicitly listed score class when present; otherwise assign absent (original Lucid code 0). A taxon_id must occur in at most one non-default class for a state.

absent.meaning: The state does not occur for the entity; this is Lucid's default categorical score.

common.meaning: The state normally or always occurs for the entity; the entity remains as a normal match.

common_misinterpreted.meaning: The state is absent but may commonly appear present through user misinterpretation.

rare.meaning: The state occurs rarely for the entity; it remains a possible match but is ranked below a common match.

rare_misinterpreted.meaning: The state is absent but may rarely appear present through user misinterpretation.

uncertain.meaning: The key author does not know whether the state occurs for the entity.

encoding.taxon_order: taxon_ids preserves the original Lucid entity vector order, including the Salticidae root entity.

concepts.notes: Chapter V recovers the Saitis group with UFBoot 100 and divides it into the Jotus and Maratus groups. Chapter V text is internally inconsistent about the number of included genera: prose refers to 13 and approximately 15, while the explicit list and male key contain 12.
Supported at UFBoot 100; explicitly comprises Jotus, Prostheclina, Tropijotus and Umbrattus.
Supported at UFBoot 100; explicitly includes Maratus, Striattus, Variattus, Saitis sensu stricto, cf. Maileus, Anablemum, Hypoblemum, Salinatus and Micromaratus.

concepts.notes: Chapter IV's explicit composition has 16 accepted species plus four incertae sedis. Chapter V's later synopsis lists only 10 accepted species and omits several Chapter IV additions or transfers, including J. remus and J. vittatus. The discrepancy is retained; this concept uses the fuller Chapter IV assertion and does not infer a silent exclusion. Jotus is recovered as monophyletic with UFBoot 100.

The Chapter V composition list itself retains Maratus expolitus, M. griseus and M. scutulatus even though the same chapter transfers them to Variattus or Hypoblemum; those contradictions are marked at the individual assertions. Maratus splendens occurs in the phylogeny but not in that composition list.

included_taxa.notes: Proposed type species.

concepts.notes: Recovered as monophyletic with UFBoot 100 and sister to Salinatus with UFBoot 100.

included_taxa.notes: Type species.

included_taxa.name: Tropijotus wondul
included_taxa.notes: Chapter III's composition line spells the epithet 'wondu'; figures and Chapter V use 'wondul'. The preferred source spelling here follows Chapter V, while the variant is retained in this note.

concepts.notes: Chapter III recovered Tropijotus as a strongly supported clade and described a relationship to Jotus plus Prostheclina. Chapter V's broader framework instead places Tropijotus as sister to Umbrattus, with UFBoot 100 for both. Both chapter assertions are retained in provenance rather than treated as identical topologies.

concepts.notes: The type species is not Australian and is morphologically dissimilar to Australian species historically placed in Salpesia. Salpesia is discussed for consideration, not confidently included in the revised Saitis group. Salpesia bimaculata is separately transferred to the proposed Umbrattus concept.
The sampled terminal is the earliest-diverging lineage of the Maratus group in Chapter V (the relevant node is UFBoot 93), but it is explicitly not confidently equated with Maileus sensu stricto.
Recovered as a deep sister lineage to the remaining sampled Prostheclina with UFBoot 99; the thesis states it may represent an undescribed genus and does not force it into Prostheclina sensu stricto.

component_evidence.rationale: Lucid itself suggests that Australian H. albovittatum sensu Keyserling represents the missing male of Maratus scutulatus; Schubert restores that species to Hypoblemum. This is a cross-source inference, not an explicit synonymy in the thesis.

mappings.notes: Do not use the identical genus spelling to collapse these concepts. The restoration and combinations proposed in the thesis are not formally published under the ICZN merely by appearing there.
mappings.rationale: The Lucid entity deliberately retains Hypoblemum but describes a confused two-name concept based on H. villosum and H. albovittatum, including an assertion that Australian material called H. albovittatum may be the missing male of Maratus scutulatus. Schubert restores a type-anchored Hypoblemum containing H. griseum, H. magnum, H. scutulatum and H. unicum, and synonymises Saitis taeniatus with H. griseum. The shared generic name and probable scutulatum connection support overlap, but the source compositions and name usages are not equivalent.

mappings.notes: This mapping records Schubert's thesis treatment as a concept reconciliation. The proposed new genera and combinations are not formally published under the ICZN merely by appearing in the thesis. Lucid labels, including apparent spelling inconsistencies, remain unmodified.
mappings.rationale: Lucid explicitly defines Maratus as a composite of peacock spiders and unrevised species inherited through the synonymised Lycidas. Schubert restricts Maratus sensu stricto and explicitly reallocates named members of the Lucid list to Anablemum, Hypoblemum, Jotus, Micromaratus, Salinatus, Striattus and Variattus. Lucid Maratus is therefore a broad legacy concept split across eight later biological concepts, not an equivalent of TC0007.

mappings.notes: The mapping is a split with unresolved residues, not a transfer of the Lucid entity wholesale. Thesis-only combinations and synonymies retain the nomenclatural caveat recorded in 04_taxon_concepts.json.
mappings.rationale: The Lucid entity is an Australian holding concept containing S. insectus, S. insulanus, S. lacustris, S. magniceps, S. mutans, S. signatus, S. taeniatus and S. virgatus. Schubert's Saitis sensu stricto is instead restricted provisionally to the Mediterranean type species S. barbipes plus S. graecus and S. tauricus. None of those three occurs in the Lucid Australian list. Schubert transfers S. mutans to Variattus, synonymises S. taeniatus with Hypoblemum griseum, synonymises S. virgatus with Umbrattus bimaculatus, and leaves or declares several other Lucid names unresolved or dubious. The concepts are therefore explicitly not equivalent and the legacy contents have multiple later dispositions.

mappings.notes: The Salpesia name is shared, but the source concepts are expressly different. The internally conflicting Umbrattus type-species assertions remain unresolved in TC0014 and are not adjudicated here.
mappings.rationale: The Lucid fact sheet explicitly says its entity describes four misplaced Australian species rather than the Seychelles type species Salpesia soricina. Schubert likewise finds no evidence that those Australian usages are congeneric with the type. Salpesia bimaculata is transferred to Umbrattus and treated as the senior synonym of Saitis virgatus; S. bicolor and S. villosa become nomina dubia, while S. squalida is incertae sedis and recovered sister to Servaea. The Lucid entity is therefore not equivalent to Schubert's type-anchored Salpesia concept and has no single later destination.

diagnostic_hints.description: Anterior median eyes bordered ventrally by light-brown to yellow scales; pale proximal palpal segments bear long light-yellow setae, while the cymbium is dark with grey-to-black setae.
Large ovate posterior spermathecae and smaller kidney-shaped anterior spermathecae extending beyond the anterior fossa margins.
Dorsal opisthosomal markings resemble those of the male.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male colour combination is useful but requires clear facial and palpal views. Female confirmation should use the epigyne.

diagnostic_hints.description: Long vivid-orange setae on the ventral femoral surface extend laterally, with a prominent blue-grey fringe on the lateral tibiae and metatarsi I.
Inner and outer embolic apices are separated proximally, unlike the proximally fused apices of T. fortiniae.
Lacks discernible dorsal opisthosomal patterning; T. fuchsia females have an anterior transverse off-white band.

species_level_identification.limitations: Female genitalia strongly resemble T. fuchsia and may not be identifiable without an associated male or molecular evidence. The female absence of a pattern is only supportive.

diagnostic_hints.description: Bicoloured fringe: a thick white transverse fringe below the anterior eye row and a vivid orange fringe above the chelicerae.
Two fused ribbon-shaped embolic apices; inner shorter, narrower and sharply pointed, outer taller, broader and truncate.
Ducts form elbowed distal sections and anterolateral lobes before reaching anterior spermathecae held tightly against the medial ducts.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male facial pattern is conspicuous. Female suggestions require epigynal examination. The spelling 'wondul' follows the species treatment; the genus composition list elsewhere has 'wondu'.

diagnostic_hints.description: Male with alternating black-and-white transverse zigzag markings; female with pale chevron-like dorsal markings.
Distinctive distal projection on the inner embolic apex.
Anterior spermathecae absent or strongly reduced, without distinct sclerotised chambers.

species_level_identification.limitations: Dorsal pattern is useful in both sexes, but female confirmation is stronger when the reduced anterior spermathecae can be examined.

diagnostic_hints.description: No long-setal fringes on legs III; two oblique white dorsal tracts are each interrupted three times, producing paired symmetrical zigzag or stepped patches.
Embolus longer than in congeners, reaching at least halfway up the cymbium in ventral view.
Larger fossae and more rounded duct diverticula than U. spectabilis, which has smaller fossae and elongate proximal receivers with an elbowed duct curve.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male dorsal pattern and absence of leg-III fringes are photographically useful. Females require epigynal comparison.

diagnostic_hints.description: Dense orange clypeal setae and long iridescent leg-III setae appearing blue to purple; compared with U. bimaculatus, whose clypeus is blue and yellow and leg-III fringe black.
Lacks the two transverse white tracts on the posterior third of the dorsal opisthosoma that occur in U. bimaculatus.
Posterior spermathecae ovate and wider than long; those of U. bimaculatus are more elongate with a medial constriction.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male colour characters are conspicuous but iridescence varies with angle. Female absence of white tracts is supportive; epigynal confirmation is preferable.

diagnostic_hints.description: Prominent bright-white tuft extends anteromedially above the anterior median eyes, combined with dense orange scales or setae on the clypeus and between the anterior eyes.
Small rounded-to-elongate diverticula are diagonally oriented anteromedially, rather than transversely as in other congeners or large and anterior as in V. zabkai.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male facial ornamentation is photographically useful. Females require epigynal examination.

diagnostic_hints.description: Elongate legs III with white setal fringes on the metatarsi; the similar V. mutans has dark-brown to black fringes.
Compact embolic disc lacks the thick proximal flange present on the more rounded disc of V. mutans.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown. White leg-III fringes support a candidate, but palpal comparison is recommended against V. mutans.

diagnostic_hints.description: Dense mat of orange scales covers the ocular quadrangle; dorsal pedipalps are distinctly bicoloured with a prominent long white fringe just before the cymbium.
Small triangular process adjacent to the base of the inner embolic apex.
Large round fossae with posteromedial openings; long ducts follow short winding, tangled paths; round diverticula lie near the anterior fossa margins.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male orange ocular scaling and bicoloured palps are useful in photographs. Female suggestions require epigynal examination.

C dissected epigyne, ventral view E dissected epigyne, dorsal view. Abbreviations: AS = anterior spermatheca, CD = copulatory duct, CO = copulatory opening, F = fossa, FD = fertilisation duct, MS = median septum, PS = posterior spermatheca. Epigynum. Epigynum with a pair of large, ovate fossae separated by a narrow septum. Posterior spermathecae medium-sized, sub-ovate, positioned at the posteromedial margin of each fossa. Copulatory ducts narrow and elongate, arising from the anteromedial margin of each posterior spermatheca, extending anteriorly before making a sharp turn at the internal anterolateral margin of each fossa, then continuing toward the anterior spermathecae. Anterior spermathecae round, smaller than the posterior spermathecae, situated just below the duct turn at the internal mediolateral margin of each fossa. Fertilization ducts slender, gently curved medially, with a slightly expanded, tapering distal portion, giving them a feather- or sickle-like appearance in dorsal view (Fig. 16C, D).

Abbreviations: AS = anterior spermathecae, CD = copulatory ducts, CO = copulatory openings, F = fossae, MS = median septum, PS = posterior spermathecae. 4.4 Discussion Our study provides the first molecular phylogenetic assessment of the genus Jotus, confirming its monophyly and helping to resolve long-standing taxonomic issues within the Saitis group. The molecular data specifically support the inclusion of Jotus chlorophthalmus comb. nov. and Jotus michaelseni comb. nov. within the genus. In the case of Jotus vittatus comb. nov., its taxonomic placement was resolved through morphological analysis following our rediscovery of the syntype series in the Museums Victoria collection. The subsequent designation of a lectotype from this material stabilises the name and confirms its placement in Jotus.
